correctness.rationale: Integer differentiation gives exactly the three characteristic-two quadrics; Euler shows the cubic lies in their ideal. Two exact affine presentations k[t,u]/(u²) cover the projective locus, gluing gives a non-split ribbon with conormal O(-6). Height three and complete-intersection adjunction produce degree 8 and genus 5. In odd characteristic the intrinsic Jacobian scheme has two reduced parameter-line charts, including characteristic 3 with F retained. The packaged symbolic checker passed and finite point searches in p=2,3,5,7 corroborated only reduced support.

originality.rationale: The claim is limited to a characteristic-sensitive identification of an established chordal cubic singular scheme with an already established balanced canonical ribbon, and the exact nonflat Hilbert-polynomial jump. Allcock gives the determinant, Deopurkar et al give precisely the abstract ribbon quadrics; no source inspected explicitly identifies their equality as the characteristic-two Jacobian scheme and compares odd characteristic. The implication from their conjunction is close and is disclosed as a significant residual risk; no novelty is claimed for the ribbon ideal itself.
residual_risks: Theorem 4.4 of Deopurkar–Fedorchuk–Swinarski contains the same three ribbon quadrics; the derivative comparison is short and a published implicit corollary may already count as coverage.
An unidentified arithmetic determinantal source could have exactly the modular Jacobian-scheme comparison.
Public mathematical-record search and recovered local history do not establish global uniqueness.

value.rationale: A natural cubic-threefold singular scheme jumps in characteristic two from a reduced rational quartic (degree 4, genus 0) to a non-split canonical genus-five ribbon (degree 8). The conormal O(-6), Hilbert jump, and explicit Jacobian realization connect two substantive geometric constructions and make an arithmetic nonflatness boundary precise rather than merely noticing rank deficiency.
